# T002: Login and logout endpoints with the login page

## Goal
When this task is done, a visitor can open `/login`, submit the form, receive the `sid` cookie and be redirected to `/`, and sign out again from any page. The routes follow `contracts/auth-api.md` to the letter, the cookie value comes from a `TokenCodec` this task implements in `src/auth/codec.ts`, and the login page is plain HTML with no build step.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a registered user, When `POST /api/login` is called with the right password, Then the response is 204 and sets an `HttpOnly` `sid` cookie whose value decodes to a session in the store.
- Given a wrong password or an unknown user, When `POST /api/login` is called, Then the response is 401 with body `{ "error": "invalid credentials" }` and no cookie is set.
- Given a signed-in user, When `POST /api/logout` is called, Then the response is 204, the session is removed from the store and the cookie is cleared.
- Given `auth.secret`, When a session id is encoded with `encode` and the result is passed to `decode`, Then the same id comes back; When any character of the signature is changed, Then `decode` returns `null` without throwing.
- Given a browser, When it opens `/login`, Then it sees a form with fields `user` and `password` and a submit button labelled "Sign in".

## Target files
- src/auth/routes.ts
- src/auth/codec.ts
- src/auth/pages/login.html
- test/auth/routes.test.ts

## Contracts
- contracts/auth-api.md
- TokenCodec (spec.md §Contracts)

## Out of scope
- Protecting other routes (T004).
- Refreshing sessions (T003).
- Styling beyond the project's existing stylesheet.

## Notes for the worker
Export `createTokenCodec(secret)` from `src/auth/codec.ts`; T004 decodes the cookie with it. Register the routes in `src/auth/routes.ts` as a function `registerAuthRoutes(server, store, codec)` so T004 can mount the middleware before them without touching this file. Read the password check from the existing `users.json` loader in `src/users.ts`; do not add a new store. The UI validator will open `/login` and submit the form, so the page must work without JavaScript.
